featured.title: Dissertation: Imagining possibilities for a more artful, embodied, and expressive math and science education
featured.description: My dissertation work focuses on exploring, alongside youth, the affordances and constraints of integrating STEM disciplines (math and science) with performing arts practices (theatre and dance). This work advances understanding of how to reframe math and science education—from unfeeling, sedentary, and objective, towards expressive, embodied, and artful.

other.title: GEM-STEP
other.description: This project explores how students learn scientific modeling and complex systems thinking through playful mixed-reality embodied science activities. I designed, implemented, and analyzed curriculum on aquatic ecosystems, decomposition, and Wetlands in an after-school club and several 5th-6th grade classrooms and led analyses on science identity, student agency, and theatrical approaches to science.

other.title: VFOI: Visualizing Funds of Identity
other.description: This project explores how network visualizations can help students to simultaneously explore their collective identities and data science concepts.

other.title: Imagination, Identity, and Power in a Children’s Museum
other.description: This project explores how through participatory design, we can design activities to support youth to engage and connect with an exhibit and be changemakers in their communities.

other.title: Foregrounding Agency versus Structure as Models for Designing Integrated Mathematics and Computational Thinking Curriculum
other.description: This project explores how integrating arts with computer science impacts youth learning
